newsitem.title: USA: Clinton seeks extra safeguards in pipeline bill.
newsitem.headline: Clinton seeks extra safeguards in pipeline bill.

text.p: President Clinton ordered extra precautions for public safety and environmentally sensitive areas when he signed a law to give oil and gas pipeline operators more flexibility in meeting safety rules, according to papers the White House released Tuesday.

In a memo, Clinton told Transportation Secretary Federico Pena that his department's Office of Pipeline Safety should continue to give full consideration to benefits of public health and safety and environmental protection -- even if the benefits have not been quantified -- in cost-benefit analyses.

The directive was issued for the pipeline safety bill, which the Office of Pipeline Safety endorsed and the Senate approved unanimously. However the bill was opposed by a number of House Democrats who said it amounted to a "deregulation" bill that weakened safety and environmental protections.
In his directive, Clinton also said the department should not authorize more than 10 pipeline risk management demonstration projects to ensure appropriate monitoring and oversight.
Also only pipeline operators "that have clear and established records of compliance" on safety and environmental protection should qualify for demonstration projects, he said.
Demonstration projects are required to "achieve superior levels of public safety and environmental protection" over existing regulations, he said.

Clinton said communities affected by demonstration projects must have meaningful public involvement, and that the demonstration projects must be subject to the government's full enforcement authority.

Clinton directed that all wetlands and aquatic areas have full environmental protections, and said the Transportation Department should consult closely with the Environmental Protection Agency in determining environmentally sensitive areas.
A spokeswoman for the Interstate National Gas Association of America said the organization was reviewing the memo, which it just had received.
"We will work within the parameters of the law," the spokeswoman said.
